q: The equipotential surfaces around a point charge $Q$ are spherical surfaces centred about the charge $Q$.
e: True. The equipotential surfaces around a point charge Q are spherical surfaces centred about the charge Q. A point charge is small enough that its own size can be ignored next to the other distances.

q: The electric lines of force are parallel to the equipotential surfaces.
e: False. The written claim is the opposite of the chapter fact. The written line says The electric lines of force are parallel to the equipotential surfaces.

q: The surface of a charged conducting sphere is an equipotential surface.
e: True. The surface of a charged conducting sphere is an equipotential surface. Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges.

q: If the surface of a conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a potential difference and the charges would move from point to point.
e: True. If the surface of a conductor is not an equipotential surface, there will be a potential difference and the charges would move from point to point. Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges.

q: Charged conductors may have any shape but their surfaces are all equipotential surfaces.
e: True. Charged conductors may have any shape but their surfaces are all equipotential surfaces. Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges.

q: The electric lines of force are perpendicular to the surface of the charged conductor.
e: True. The electric lines of force are perpendicular to the surface of the charged conductor. Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges.

q: The work done is zero in bringing a charge from one point to another point on the equipotential surface.
e: True. The work done is zero in bringing a charge from one point to another point on the equipotential surface. Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.
